card.title: Who We Used to Be
card.instruction: Perform the version of yourself that belonged to this relationship before it changed, and treat old chemistry as still recoverable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wore the scarf from our first photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't fit your coat anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It fits the person you met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to be that person.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just until dessert. He knew how to make you laugh.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 wears the first-photo scarf, A3 identifies it with the old self, and A5 asks to keep that self through dessert to recover the ability to make B laugh.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's current coat mismatch informs A3's old-person fit; B4's permission to change leads A5 to request temporary return to the earlier chemistry.

relationship.evidence: B2 notices a present mismatch and B4 offers release from performing the former self.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's permission to stop as the occasion to ask for a little longer; the development is emotional rather than a large event.

specificity.evidence: A1-A3 establish an old shared photograph and a consciously revived earlier version of A.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's dessert limit and remembered laughter are restrained and connected to B4's reassurance.
